title: The normal human
unit: head: one head height, crown to chin

frames.upper: heights in heads measured down from the crown (head and torso stay about 4 heads in every build)
frames.lower: heights as a fraction of crotch height above the floor (legs take the extra length in tall builds)
frames.widths: full widths in heads, seen from the front; depths in heads, seen from the side
frames.stature: for scoring, every landmark is also given as a fraction of standing height from the floor

sources.title: Anatomy of the Human Body (Gray's Anatomy), 20th ed.
sources.author: Henry Gray, rev. W. H. Lewis

sources.title: Artistic Anatomy / Canon des proportions du corps humain
sources.author: Paul Richer
sources.access: original public domain; canon as tabulated by Proko's average-figure lesson

sources.title: A Handbook of Anatomy for Art Students
sources.author: Arthur Thomson

sources.title: Figure Drawing for All It's Worth
sources.author: Andrew Loomis
sources.access: publisher edition (Titan, 2011) and Proko's idealistic-figure lesson; not reproduced

sources.title: How to Draw Comics the Marvel Way
sources.author: Stan Lee and John Buscema
sources.access: publisher edition and published summaries; not reproduced

chin.name: Chin
chin.find: bottom of the jaw; one head down from the crown

pit.name: Pit of the neck
pit.find: notch at the top of the breastbone, between the collarbones

acromion.name: Shoulder point
acromion.find: bony tip of the shoulder at the outer end of the collarbone

nipple.name: Chest line
nipple.find: two heads down; the nipple line on a man, the bust apex on a woman

ribs.name: Bottom of the ribcage
ribs.find: lowest edge of the rib arch at the side

elbow.name: Elbow
elbow.find: point of the elbow with the arm hanging; level with the bottom of the ribs or the waist

waist.name: Waist
waist.find: narrowest part of the trunk; higher on a woman

navel.name: Navel
navel.find: three heads down; just above the top of the hip bone

iliac.name: Top of the hip bone
iliac.find: the iliac crest; the one stable hip landmark (Bridgman)

asis.name: Front hip point
asis.find: the bony point at the front of the pelvis (ASIS)

wrist.name: Wrist
wrist.find: with the arm hanging, at the level of the crotch

troch.name: Hip joint bump
troch.find: the great trochanter: the widest bony point of the hips, outer thigh

crotch.name: Crotch
crotch.find: the middle of the body's height sits at the pubic bone, just above it

fingertip.name: Fingertips
fingertip.find: with the arm hanging, at mid-thigh

knee.name: Knee
knee.find: bottom of the kneecap; halfway from the front hip point to the floor (Richer)

calf.name: Widest calf
calf.find: inner calf bulges lower than the outer

ankle.name: Ankle
ankle.find: outer ankle bone; the inner ankle sits higher (Bridgman)

male-average.label: Man, average
male-average.notes: Richer's average man. Shoulders twice the head; hips narrower than shoulders (about 1.3 to 1).

female-average.label: Woman, average
female-average.notes: Narrower shoulders, wider and deeper pelvis, higher waist, the trochanters are the widest point; shoulders and hips about equal (1.05 to 1).

heroic.label: Heroic
heroic.notes: Loomis's heroic figure (8.5 heads) and the Marvel Way hero (about 8.75): the extra length goes into the legs, the shoulders reach 2.33 heads on a man, the head looks smaller.

skinny.label: Skinny
skinny.notes: Same skeleton, less on it: joints read big against thin limbs, the collarbones, ribs and hip points show.

heavy.label: Heavy
heavy.notes: Same skeleton, more soft mass. Men carry it on the belly in front; women on the hips, thighs and seat. Joints and the head stay their size.

shoulder_to_hip.source: Richer; Wikipedia 'Body proportions' (lateral widths, means 1.18 and 1.03)

tolerance.note: heights within 0.15 head of the canon, widths within 12 percent
